title: October 13: future-sufficient memory, trainable response graphs, inverse mandalas and material fossils
summary: Four distinct 13 October repositories enter the wall. ResearchQuestion isolates the exact future-sufficiency condition and benchmarks learned codes against switched ERA/linear PEM; SihtiResponseGraph trains an image-conditioned response operator for planar glyph rotation, with a small one-seed graph-versus-vector pilot; InverseMandala proves nonlinear max-symmetry ambiguity and compares complementary versus coded views; Kerrostuma makes a simulated toroidal crust that retains formation history and tests approximate predictive closure under wait/melt interventions. The connections are documented mechanism reuse or conceptual comparisons, not one discovered AI architecture. Small synthetic tests and their negative results remain visible.

nodes.claim: A browser-rendered seeded toroidal material world: quench a curved-surface Swift–Hohenberg crust under an initially hidden cooling/spin law; grow GelatinIsland-style carriers and conductive gel on defects; probe the present crust for information about past formation and future wait/melt responses.
nodes.survived: Headless WebGL-to-CPU fixture matches the specified crust evolution; 8/8 fresh synthetic worlds classified fast versus slow cooling using a frozen calibration. On 5/18 worlds whose spin exceeded a no-wind null threshold, inferred direction was correct 5/5 (selective cases only). Grown conductive gel transmits identical pulses to 4005–6705 cells versus 176–243 after shuffling. For 36 distinct world/age histories, the compact crust census predicts held-out next census under an 80-step wait (R² defects 0.94; coherence 0.92), but this is a finite-sample predictive fit rather than a proof of exact state closure.
nodes.killed: The field is a toy with supplied physics, artistic optics, fixed known age in the principal calibration and limited test worlds—not a planetary model. Spin is mostly unreadable outside fast-cooled worlds; the proposed re-melt probe heals from rim templating and fails as an independent clock, and predicting scar-minus-surrounding response fails (R² -0.14 from the basic census). No unique age/cooling-rate inversion or exact closed quotient is established.
nodes.era: Temporal fossils in physical-shaped procedural worlds

nodes.claim: When does an encoder retain enough state to answer and update future queries? An exact 32D nonlinear mechanism isolates a four-coordinate future-sufficient quotient, and a bridge-feedback world where five coordinates are necessary. A second learned experiment hides the latent basis and trains small prediction memories; a switched-system ERA and post-hoc prediction-error refinement test classical competitors.
nodes.survived: In the constructed v1 world, all eight fixed gates pass: future readout Jacobian rank is 4 without bridge feedback and 5 with it; predictive four-state NRMSE rises to 0.274 only in the bridge world while exact five-state future error is about 4.5e-16. On 2 independent synthetic apparatus seeds v2 learned 5D prediction scores 0.179/0.157 six-step NRMSE (closed/bridge). Post-hoc linear ERA+PEM beats learned 5D on closed (0.156 vs 0.179) while learned tanh wins on bridge (0.157 vs 0.180); pure switched ERA loses both.
nodes.killed: The v1 exact quotient was engineered using privileged hidden coordinates, not learned. V2 is a new synthetic apparatus with supervised query labels and only two seeds; the learned fifth coordinate also helps in the closed world, so bridge identification is not proved. Pure ERA's poorer long rollout is not a refutation of classical realization theory; the linear PEM upgrade was explicitly post-hoc. No images, neurons, or general-purpose pretrained AI were evaluated.

nodes.claim: A compact trainable image-response graph: a synthetic 32×32 coloured glyph writes 896 quantized image-specific edge conductances on an 8×8 lattice. The observed image activity is cleared; a new spatial ping propagates through those conductances and a decoder answers one of four planar quarter-turn queries. Comparison stores an equal-byte vector rather than edge conductances.
nodes.survived: One seeded pilot (seed 7, 1200 training steps; 1024 training and 128 held-out glyphs) measured held-out MSE 0.023825 (16.23 dB) for the uint8 response graph versus 0.025985 (15.85 dB) for the 896-byte vector and 0.033369 (14.77 dB) for a fixed-graph control. The graph wins on three rotated views but not the unrotated one; tests cover cleared-state repeated queries, swapped memories, masked writes and gradients. The operator stores information that a fresh probe can read. Follow-up frozen-writer tests probe a previously missed tiny mark: a separately trained mark-aware reader reduces graph mark-pixel RGB MSE from 0.04652 to 0.02644 on 256 new synthetic objects, versus 0.03308 for an erased-mark-trained graph and 0.02832 for an equal-byte vector with its own mark-aware head. Shuffling or erasing the mark before writing hurts mark recovery, indicating part of the distinction survives in stored bytes even when the initial renderer blurs it.
nodes.killed: The experiment learns only deterministic planar quarter-turns, not previously unseen 3D geometry, real-world video or faithful identity after occlusion. The original RGB renderer blurs the tiny distinguishing mark; a separately trained reader can partially recover it, but mark geometry and colour remain imperfect. One seed, unequal shared parameter/compute overhead and a graph consisting of 896 stored bytes do not establish a reliable model advantage, an efficient codec or biologically faithful dendrites.

nodes.claim: Extracts the nonlinear image-mixing step of January's 2MandalaTools: rotated copies, odd-copy reflections, and per-pixel maximum. Tests inverse ambiguity with an exact pair of different source images producing identical N=3,7,16 mandalas; implements blind inverse reconstruction, winning-layer provenance diagnostics, a browser lab and fixed pre-max digital mask/contrast/center interventions.
nodes.survived: The exact collision proves the single and multiple high-symmetry observations do not uniquely identify every source. A blind solver can almost perfectly re-render the N=16 face mandala (45.33 dB) yet recover the source poorly (10.31 dB). Three symmetry views improve the synthetic face to 18.33 dB. V2 equal three-view comparison across three synthetic scenes: mean source PSNR 15.45 dB for N=3,7,16 versus 13.73 for fixed coded masks. Digital pre-max masks expose the otherwise invisible one-pixel collision (0.1625 largest 0–1 output difference).
nodes.killed: An argmax map only identifies the winning copy, not the suppressed pixel values. Coded masks break this particular ambiguity but do not beat extra symmetry views for overall reconstruction; contrast inversion also exposes the collision. Results concern three noise-free 64×64 drawings with known forward law, solver approximate OpenCV interpolation and no trainable image prior. Independent masks for each virtual layer cannot be treated as a realizable Varjoluotain shadow plate, and neither visual fit nor very high forward PSNR proves unique source recovery.

edges.why: InverseMandala explicitly extracts and reproduces frequency_mandalas3.py's rotation, alternating mirror and pixelwise-max compositing stage. It isolates the inverse problem instead of repeating the original FFT equalizer or false-colour display.

The inverse mandala's v2 experiment explicitly contrasts coded pre-max digital measurements with Varjoluotain's occluder-defined light transport. Both test whether modifying a measurement exposes distinctions, but the independently addressable virtual masks here are not physical periscopy.

SihtiResponseGraph names Sihti's image-conditioned neighbor weights as inspiration, then trains a new image-specific graph whose read starts from cleared input-independent activity; the source does not claim direct inheritance of Sihti's purifier code.

Both study a propagation geometry that retains information from past input instead of solely from instantaneous pixels, but this is a conceptual comparison rather than a documented copied implementation.

ResearchQuestion explicitly calls its telescoping full-state decomposition Sihti-like bookkeeping and distinguishes this construction from Sihti's original dyadic diffusion. The experiment asks which discarded residue affects future queries, not how to reconstruct an image.

Kerrostuma explicitly credits CrystalMoon for its Swift–Hohenberg material/visual idea, then simulates quench-written patterns on a curved torus. This is a documented conceptual/mathematical descent, not asserted file-level code inheritance.
Kerrostuma's 20,480 carriers lay gel veins, and the project explicitly credits GelatinIsland for carrier-to-conducting-network dynamics. A shuffled-gel control tests the resulting conduction.

motifs.title: A seen image can store information in a future response operator
motifs.description: Sihti fixes graph topology but writes per-edge conductances from local pixel similarity; SighImageFactorization explores learning history-conditioned relations; SihtiResponseGraph trains an equal-byte stored conductance field so that a fresh spatial ping can recover a planar glyph rotation. This is demonstrated on a small seeded 2D glyph task, not unseen 3D structure, pretrained vision or a general compression advantage.

motifs.title: A good present readout may not be a sufficient state for the next intervention
motifs.description: ResearchQuestion constructs a causal feedback bridge whose influence appears only after subsequent actions and compares finite learned and classical predictors. Kerrostuma separately measures how formation history survives in an evolving crust: a small census predicts waiting responses on a 36-world pilot but not remelt-scar residuals, and hidden law labels need not outperform present-state observations. This is a shared conditional sufficiency test, not proof that a planet and a network implement one memory mechanism.

motifs.title: Nonlinear symmetry can conceal information; independent measurements can reveal it
motifs.description: 2MandalaTools manufactures repeated image structure by max-mixing rotated and mirrored copies. InverseMandala proves a source collision and tests how multiple views, per-branch coded masks and contrast change recoverability. Varjoluotain uses a distinct physical light-transport operator with an occluding plate. The connection is intervention-dependent observability, explicitly not an equivalence between digital per-layer masks and a real shadow plate.
